def is_plain_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when name is a single non-empty path component that cannot leave the directory: no separators, no NUL, and not "." or ".."."""
    ex is_plain_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_plain_name("../secret") == False
    ex is_plain_name("..") == False
    ex is_plain_name(".") == False
    ex is_plain_name("") == False
    ex is_plain_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_plain_name("a\\b") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    for c in name.chars():
        if c == "/" or c == "\\" or c == "\0":
            return False
    return True

def plain_names(names: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """The names that pass is_plain_name, in order."""
    ex plain_names(["a", "../b", "c"]) == ["a", "c"]
    ex plain_names(["..", "/x"]) == []
    return [n.copy() for n in names if is_plain_name(n)]

def first_readable(names: list[str]) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the first file in names that can be read from the directory `notes`, or "" when none can.
    Names are untrusted: reads happen only under `with fs = fs.sub("notes")`, and names that are not plain single-component names are skipped.
    Missing or unreadable files are skipped."""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        for n in plain_names(names):
            text = fs.read_text(n) else continue
            return text
    return ""
